title: Tenure Incentives vs Risk-Taking
bottleneck: The tenure track demands a steady stream of publications in a researcher's 30s — the years of peak creativity — punishing anyone who spends years on a hard, uncertain problem. The result is rational risk-aversion at exactly the career stage when boldness historically paid off. Playing it safe in one's 30s becomes rational career strategy, selecting against the boldest thinkers.
why_it_blocks: Tenure was meant to protect intellectual risk; its pursuit now discourages it. The boldest thinkers learn to disguise ambition as incrementalism.
current_state: Tenure-clock extensions and alternative tracks exist but do not change the underlying publication-counting evaluation. Alternative evaluation based on long-term impact rather than publication velocity has been proposed but rarely adopted. Evaluation reform is the lever; everything else follows from what gets rewarded.

sources.title: Evidence and the Design and Reform of Scientific Institutions (Nintil)
